title: AI Replaced 75% of Work for Software Engineers & Data Scientists - here's what's left
summary: Two practitioners chat about which parts of SWE/DS work AI automates: coding yes, design and soft skills no.

assertions.quote: as soon as you ask it to like do something more complex or like take in the context or the business of the product ... that's where it fails

verdicts.note: Benchmarks and field studies show strong performance on well-specified, common tasks and weaker results on context-heavy, novel logic.

assertions.quote: in order to validate what AI is spitting out, you actually need to know if the code ... is correct

verdicts.note: Studies show novices accept incorrect AI code more often; verifying output requires domain and code literacy.
The review concludes that skill in verification, constraint specification and review may matter as much as authoring skill, and that the central risk is a verification gap.

assertions.quote: great for like prototyping, but scaling it to like a larger um user base, like that's when it starts to fail

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.
The 47-source review finds evidence strongest for prototyping and UI work and weakest for production. The break-down half is mostly unstudied, not shown.

assertions.quote: you actually don't need a software engineer to like build the first prototype

verdicts.note: Tools like Lovable, v0, Replit let non-developers produce working prototypes; widely observed.
45% of sources stress accessibility for novices and non-programmers. That evidence is mostly grey literature and centered on prototypes.

assertions.quote: system design is a place where soft engineers will thrive

verdicts.note: Humans still own constraints and tradeoffs, but models can now propose reasonable designs when given context; the gap is narrowing.

20 of 47 sources (43%) describe expert use in which developers speed up routine implementation 'while retaining responsibility for architectural reasoning and verification'; this is descriptive, not a test of AI design ability.
Anthropic: engineers keep high-level design and 'taste' tasks, but call that boundary a moving target, and Claude Code design/planning usage grew from 1% to 10% in six months.

assertions.quote: senior software engineers ... they're going to be super high in demand

verdicts.note: Hiring data (e.g. Stanford 'canaries' 2025) shows junior roles hit harder than senior, but evidence that senior demand rose is weaker.

assertions.quote: Some of them even allow you to use AI tools in interviews

verdicts.note: Some companies allow AI or changed formats (e.g. Meta AI-enabled rounds), but LeetCode-style screens remain common.

assertions.quote: our jobs will evolve and not be replaced

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.
Requirements, stakeholder alignment and judgment remain hard to delegate; plausible though not strictly testable.
